solution: Solution: Write each pair as a single cosine: $4\cos 2x-4\sqrt{3}\sin 2x=8\cos\left(2x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$ $\cos 3x-\sqrt{3}\sin 3x=2\cos\left(3x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$ $\cos x-\sqrt{3}\sin x=2\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$ So the equation becomes $8\cos\left(2x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+2\cos\left(3x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+2\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=0$ Divide by $2$ : $4\cos\left(2x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+\cos\left(3x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=0$ Use $\cos A+\cos B=2\cos\frac{A+B}{2}\cos\frac{A-B}{2}$ : $\cos\left(3x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=2\cos\left(2x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\cos x$ Hence $4\cos\left(2x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+2\cos\left(2x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\cos x=0$ $2\cos\left(2x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)(2+\cos x)=0$ Since $2+\cos x>0$ , we get $\cos\left(2x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=0$ Thus $2x+\frac{\pi}{3}=n\pi+\frac{\pi}{2}$ $2x=n\pi+\frac{\pi}{6}$ $x=\frac{n\pi}{2}+\frac{\pi}{12}$ , where $n\in\mathbb{Z}$ Therefore the general solution is option C. © examsnet.com

solution: Solution: Take $A$ as the origin, and let $\overline{AB}=\mathbf b$ and $\overline{AC}=\mathbf c$ . Since $ABC$ is equilateral, $|\mathbf b|=|\mathbf c|=a$ and $\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf c=a^2\cos 60^\circ=\frac{a^2}{2}$ . Given $\overline{AB}=3\overline{AM}$ , we get $\overline{AM}=\frac{1}{3}\overline{AB}=\frac{\mathbf b}{3}$ . Thus $\overline{CM}=\overline{AM}-\overline{AC}=\frac{\mathbf b}{3}-\mathbf c$ . Given $\overline{AN}=K\overline{AC}=K\mathbf c$ . Thus $\overline{BN}=\overline{AN}-\overline{AB}=K\mathbf c-\mathbf b$ . Since $\overline{BN}\perp\overline{CM}$ , $(K\mathbf c-\mathbf b)\cdot\left(\frac{\mathbf b}{3}-\mathbf c\right)=0.$ Expanding, $\frac{K}{3}\mathbf c\cdot\mathbf b-K\mathbf c\cdot\mathbf c-\frac{1}{3}\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf b+\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf c=0.$ Substitute $\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf c=\frac{a^2}{2}$ and $\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf b=\mathbf c\cdot\mathbf c=a^2$ : $\frac{K}{3}\cdot\frac{a^2}{2}-Ka^2-\frac{a^2}{3}+\frac{a^2}{2}=0.$ Divide by $a^2$ : $\frac{K}{6}-K-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{2}=0.$ So, $-\frac{5K}{6}+\frac{1}{6}=0\implies 5K=1\implies K=\frac{1}{5}.$ Therefore the correct option is $\frac{1}{5}$ . © examsnet.com

Substitute $v^2=\frac{GM}{2R}$ : $\frac{1}{2}m\left(\frac{GM}{2R}\right)-\frac{GMm}{R}=-\frac{GMm}{R+h}$ . This simplifies to $\frac{GMm}{4R}-\frac{GMm}{R}=-\frac{GMm}{R+h}$ . So $-\frac{3GMm}{4R}=-\frac{GMm}{R+h}$ . Canceling $GMm$ gives $\frac{3}{4R}=\frac{1}{R+h}$ . Thus $R+h=\frac{4R}{3}$ , so $h=\frac{R}{3}$ .
